title: Intent/Application spec
description: The desired-state payload for an application Intent (charter §2.4, ADR-0023). v2 types `port` (ADR-0118 follow-up). A SIBLING VERSION rather than an edit to v1 because tightening a type is a BREAKING change — an Intent declaring `port: 443` parsed under v1 and does not under v2 — and the registry's convention is a new file per version (the resolver keys by kind and takes the newest, so v1 stays as a pin row for history while v2 is what validates). Still deliberately OPEN (additionalProperties: true): Intent/Application is a generic kind whose spec carries application-specific values — the app-cert demo's commonName, for instance — and closing it would force core to know every application's configuration fields, the ontology creep §1.1 and §9 forbid. Blueprints reference spec fields by explicit lookup ({{.spec.package}}).

chartVersion.description: Desired version of the deliverable for a CHART-delivered application, as a STRING — the same load-bearing type argument `port` records below: contracts/facets/app.deliverable declares the OBSERVED version as a string and nothing coerces between types (ADR-0118 D1). Typed here rather than left to additionalProperties because a shipping Blueprint route reads it (estate/blueprints/podinfo.yaml) and because the `port` field records what leaving it untyped costs — a number parses cleanly and fails at facet comparison, which is a full round-trip away. Adding it is not the tightening this file's own header warns about: no declaration in the repo used this key before the one added alongside it, so nothing that parsed stops parsing.

port.description: Desired listen port, as a STRING — the type is load-bearing, not stylistic. contracts/facets/app.config.schema.json declares the OBSERVED port as a string, and a compiled expectation from this spec is compared against that observed value; nothing coerces between types (ADR-0118 D1), so the two must agree or they are never comparable. Typed here because two shipping Blueprint routes read it (estate/blueprints/web-server.yaml and the app-cert demo) — and because leaving it untyped cost a full cluster round-trip: an Intent declaring a number parsed cleanly and failed only at facet write-back with '/port: got number, want string'.
